 After product recall, Once Upon a Farm hit with new false advertising lawsuit
 The food producer is facing more litigation in California, this time over its potentially hazardous soft-baked bar products.
 Kayvon Bumpus 
 / November 17, 2026 Link copied 
 Once Upon a Farm’s Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bar product line was recalled due to a choking hazard. (U.S. Food and Drug Administration) (CN) — Oat bars that reportedly caused choking incidents involving toddlers have created a hard-to-swallow legal situation for Once Upon a Farm.
 The Bay Area-based children’s food manufacturer was sued in federal court Tuesday by three customers who say the company falsely labeled its “Tractor Wheels Organic Soft-Baked Bar” product, which was recalled last month.
 Once Upon a Farm is already facing litigation in the same judicial venue — U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California — in response to it advertising a technically vegetable-less product as a “Fruit & Veggie Blend.”
 The three plaintiffs in the Tractor Wheels oat bar case live in Oregon, Washington, D.C., and New York respectively. They seek to form a nationwide class of customers who purchased the bars within the last four years, as well as sub-classes for each location they represent.
 On Oct. 30, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration warned consumers that the oat bars could cause “potentially fatal” choking in toddlers.
 “When chewed, the product reportedly forms a dry, sticky mass that standard choking interventions — including back blows and the Heimlich maneuver — may fail to dislodge,” the agency stated in an online alert. “Some reported choking incidents have required emergency response intervention and hospital observation.”
 Days later, Once Upon a Farm issued a full recall of the Tractor Wheels product line.
 “We know that parents place their trust in us every time they buy one of our products. We fell short of that, and that is why we are taking these aggressive actions,” the company said.
 The putative class representatives called that recall “woefully inadequate” and argued Once Upon a Farm had made “incredibly lucrative” profits off sales of the oat bars by specifically marketing them as safe and healthy for toddlers.
 “The FDA has instructed parents that instead of little toddler hands, these products belong in the trash,” the plaintiffs, represented by Smith Krivoshey, say in the complaint.
 “The front and back labels of the products omit any mention of the fact that the products are not suitable to be consumed by toddlers and that they pose a serious and potentially fatal choking hazard if consumed by toddlers,” the plaintiffs added, accusing the food manufacturer of violating California, Oregon, District of Columbia and New York consumer protection laws.
 Once Upon a Farm did not respond to requests for comment.
